mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term discounting effect that reduces the present value of expected equity returns, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 4% in the prior month (p-value < 0.05 in a regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) creates a dual labor-market weakness that depresses corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when PAYEMS up and HOUST up (independent t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% signals accelerating economic activity that outpaces risk premia, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when INDPRO acceleration persists (F-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for two consecutive months reduces the Fed's incentive to raise rates, lowering discount rates and supporting equity valuations, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL < 2.0% for two months (robustness across 5-year window).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in three months, it signals labor market strength that typically precedes rate hikes, which compresses forward discounting and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% after two consecutive months above 4.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when UNRATE < 4.5% for only one month (not sustained).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) indicates a shift toward services dominance, lowering growth expectations and producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while RSAFS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when PAYEMS up and RSAFS up (independent regression, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the 12-week moving average of consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 225 suggests disinflation that persists for at least 3 months, reducing policy tightening risk and supporting equity valuations for a 60-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL 12-week MA falls below 225 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL MA > 225 for 3 months (robustness across 5-year sample).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a decline in consumer demand (HOUST) within the same month creates a supply-demand imbalance that elevates risk aversion and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO up and HOUST up (independent t-test, p > 0.05).
